body:
#2008 REWORKED AND IT IS EXACTLY THE SPLIT, with one part better than I asked for. Reviewed, not merged — the drain is at phase 1 on BUG-1303, so the drive owns it.

+47/-3, down from +92/-6. Contention classification stays, EINTR handling gone.

THE BETTER PART: the only surviving mention of `Interrupted` is a NEGATIVE test — `rejects_non_contention_failures` asserts an interrupted error is NOT classified as contention. I asked for the speculative handling to be removed. Removing it AND pinning that the classifier cannot over-match into it is the stronger move, because the characteristic failure of a contention check is that it grows to swallow things it should not. That is the lane improving on the direction rather than just following it.

All three lock sites now call the shared `is_lock_contended`, which was the original criterion 1 — one definition, three callers, no open-coded copies left to drift apart. And `classifies_windows_raw_lock_violation_on_linux_ci` proves the Windows path by injection on Linux CI, so it is verifiable without waiting on the matrix.

I stated on the PR exactly what it now claims and what it does not: the Windows cause is established by observation, and this change addresses it by mechanism rather than by correlation with a green run. It does not claim the Linux flake is solved, nothing observed points at a cause for that, and a Windows contention code cannot explain a Linux race. That half of BUG-1303 stays open.

MY HOLDS ARE NOW ACTUALLY ENFORCED, incidentally — #2003 and #2006 both flipped to BLOCKED once I applied the labels. Which is its own small confirmation that they were not blocking anything before.

Nothing else moved this tick. No mail, no rework on #2006 or #2009.
